newsitem.title: USA: Carnival sees Costa tender in May.
newsitem.headline: Carnival sees Costa tender in May.

text.p: Carnival Corp chairman Micky Arison said on Monday the cruise-ship giant expects to tender in early May with partner Airtours Plc of Britain for the outstanding shares of Costa Crociere SpA of Italy.

Arison told reporters after Carnival's annual meeting that regulators in Italy should shortly approve the tender offer and that the transaction, assuming approval by European Union antitrust officials, should close by early summer.
"That's not an issue," Arison said of possible antitrust objections to Carnival buying Costa, the leading cruise ship operator in the Mediterranean.

The biggest cruise-ship group in the world, Carnival would along with Airtours, the second largest tour vendor in Britain, and Costa have 14-15 cruise ships in the Mediterranean during the summer high season.
Carnival and Airtours announced in January that they would pay about $300 million for Costa and had agreed to buy 51 percent of the company from a controlling syndicate.

Arison told the shareholders Carnival expected many cost savings such as bulk purchases of supplies and other benefits for the ships after the combination with Costa but declined to discuss specific actions.
